transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Derek (Redwood SE), Lena (CSM), Jared (MedSpace Head of ML), Priya (MedSpace SRE), Anika (PM)

Summary:
Quick implementation kickoff to align on onboarding plan for MedSpace's pilot with Redwood Dedicated (reserved sandbox). Confirm security requirements, VPC networking, expected load, and next steps around SSO and pilot timeline.

Topics:
- Pilot scope and success criteria
- Network/VPC and firewall needs
- SSO, audit logs, and compliance docs
- Benchmarking and sample workloads
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samira from Redwood, AE for MedSpace. Quick round of intros so we know who's on — Derek, CSM Lena, and then MedSpace team?
[00:12] Jared: Hi, Jared here, head of ML at MedSpace.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, SRE.
[00:17] Anika: Anika, product.
[00:19] Derek: Derek Wu, solutions engineer on the inference team, excited to dig in.
[00:23] Samira: Great. The goal for today is to confirm scope and what we need to provision for your pilot: sandbox Dedicated instance, VPC peering or Private, SSO, and any compliance checks. We'll also capture milestones. Should be about 45 minutes.

[00:45] Derek: I'll start with a high level of the infra options — for pilots most customers choose either Hosted with private data retention or a Dedicated sandbox. Since you mentioned wanting isolation and predictable perf, Dedicated sounds right. We can do a dedicated pool in us-west-2 and set up a VPC peering or private link.
[01:05] Jared: Yeah isolation is important — we handle PHI-ish metadata in some flows, though the content is de-identified mostly. We need audit logs and KMS integration if possible.
[01:17] Lena: We support KMS and customer-managed keys for Private/Private-mode; for Dedicated there are options. We'll include security docs.

[01:33] Priya: On networking — our stack is in an AWS VPC and we prefer VPC peering rather than public endpoints. What are the firewall rules and CIDRs you need?
[01:42] Derek: We'll share a VPC diagram. Typically we need outbound to a set of Redwood-managed IPs, and if you do peering, we'll request route table entries. Firewall ports are mostly 443, and some control plane ports for management but those can be restricted. I'll include exact CIDR ranges in the doc.

[02:05] Anika: Timeline — we want a pilot running in the next 3 weeks if possible. Is that realistic?
[02:12] Samira: Yes that's realistic if we get the onboarding checklist items quickly: SSO details, security contact, and the networking ticket. We'll aim for provision by Feb 16 and benchmark by Feb 23.

[02:32] Derek: On benchmarks — to size the pool we'll need expected QPS, average sequence length, and concurrency. Even ballpark numbers help. Also whether you'll use streaming or sync generation.
[02:44] Jared: For the initial pilot it's low throughput — maybe 10 requests/sec peak, average 120 tokens per request, concurrency around 6. We'll run a production load test later.

[03:02] Priya: For compliance, do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 docs? Our security team will want them.
[03:08] Lena: Yes, we will share SOC 2 and ISO docs, as well as our data retention and redaction policies. Also we'll provide a sample auditable log format.

[03:24] Derek: A couple of notes — when people say "KV cache" some docs list as "K-V cash" in older transcripts, sorry — but practically we support prefix caching and token KV reuse in the runtime to cut token costs. For your workloads prefix reuse might help.
[03:40] Jared: Good to know. We'll probably use cached prompts for triage flows.

[03:50] Anika: SSO — we use Okta. We need to know what SAML attributes Redwood expects and whether SCIM provisioning is supported.
[03:58] Lena: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We'll send the SSO spec with the ACS URL and required attributes.

[04:12] Priya: Any restrictions around model variants? We expect to try an open model and a quantized variant. Do you offer quantized serving in Dedicated?
[04:20] Derek: Yes, we have quantized paths and can run optimized kernels on the Dedicated runtime. We'll provide performance profiles. For fallback, we can do model routing if capacity is constrained.

[04:35] Jared: About data residency — can the logs and telemetry be stored in a particular region? We need EU residency for some customers though MedSpace is US-first.
[04:44] Samira: For Dedicated we can pin region to us-west-2 as requested; logs can be routed to your KMS and choice of region for storage. We'll include configuration options.

[05:02] Anika: Ok so immediate asks from us — a) SSO setup info, b) VPC peering instructions and expected IPs, c) security questionnaire if any.
[05:11] Samira: We'll send those. Derek, can you own the networking doc and bench plan?
[05:15] Derek: Yep. I'll attach a sample firewall matrix and the peering diagram.

[05:25] Lena: I'll open the pilot ticket in our onboarding system and provision a sandbox project. I'll also attach SOC2 and ISO docs.

[05:32] Priya: One more on monitoring — what observability do we get out of the box? Token-level latency, per-route metrics?
[05:39] Derek: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, request traces, and error analysis. We can push metrics to your Datadog or a webhook as well.

[05:55] Jared: For benchmarking, can Redwood run a sample perf test or do we run it?
[06:00] Derek: We typically provide a benchmark harness; we can run it together or provide instructions. For Dedicated we can run a baseline and share token/s cost and latency numbers with your sample prompts.

[06:18] Anika: Who's the main contact for the pilot on Redwood side?
[06:22] Samira: I'm the AE point, Derek SE for technical, and Lena will manage onboarding ops. Use the pilot ticket for requests.

[06:32] Jared: On security docs, do you have a shared NDA or data processing agreement templates? We'll need DPAs for handling any customer data even if de-identified.
[06:40] Lena: We have DPA and standard enterprise contracts. I'll loop in legal if needed — I'll attach the DPA and our standard terms.

[06:52] Priya: A small note — our infra team will likely require a temporary test account for peering verification. Is that okay?
[06:57] Derek: Totally fine. We'll create temporary test endpoints and credentials for smoke tests.

[07:06] Samira: Recap — deliverables from Redwood: onboarding checklist + security docs (Samira/Lena), VPC peering diagram and firewall CIDRs + benchmark plan (Derek), sandbox provisioning (Lena). From MedSpace: SSO metadata, security contacts, and sample prompts/QPS. Timeline target: provision sandbox by Feb 16, initial bench by Feb 23.

[07:30] Anika: Sounds good. One more thing — pricing for Dedicated sandbox? We discussed estimates in sales deck but need a simple summary to share with finance.
[07:38] Samira: I'll include a concise pricing summary in the onboarding email along with license terms.

[07:46] Jared: Perfect. If anything blocks the networking side we'll escalate to Priya.
[07:50] Priya: Yep.

[07:54] Samira: All right we'll follow up with the onboarding packet and open the pilot ticket. Any final questions?
[08:00] Anika: No, that's it for now.
[08:02] Jared: Thanks all.
[08:04] Derek: Thanks.
[08:06] Lena: Thanks everyone, will share docs shortly.

[08:12] (call ends)

Action items (restated):
- Samira: Send onboarding checklist, pricing, and SSO docs by 2026-02-14.
- Derek: Share VPC peering diagram, CIDR/firwall matrix, and benchmark plan by 2026-02-19.
- Lena: Open pilot ticket and provision sandbox by 2026-02-16; attach SOC2/ISO and DPA.
- Jared: Send sample prompt set and expected QPS by 2026-02-18.
